published_source_followup.title: [Items][P2][Design] Define Training Grounds, affordable retraining and Item Finder rewards
published_source_followup.body:
Follow-up to #930, tracked by #919. Depends on repair gate #929.

## Player goal

Let a player develop a chosen Pokémon into a useful battle build through deliberate, repeatable training, and change that build affordably. Adapt the activity to a text MUCK: a few worthwhile sessions, clear feedback and opportunities for roleplay or coaching. A dependable training route must remain available when other players have used a source or the Item Finder has been unlucky.

The agreed direction replaces this issue's previous three-shop proposal. The old prices, initial quantities, counter names and recipe identities are superseded proposals. This issue now owns the training/retraining design and supplementary item-access plan; it does not claim those activities are implemented.

## Training Grounds

Proposed player flow: choose a Pokémon → choose a stat → complete a short training session or NPC sparring challenge → inspect the exact saved training gain and remaining capacity.

- Make chosen-stat EV progress predictable for a completed qualifying session. Keep it repeatable and usable solo; roleplay, coaching or cooperative play can accompany it without requiring another player or staff member to be online.
- Keep the number of sessions reasonable for text combat. Avoid hundreds of repetitive fights, repeated single-point commands, or progress dependent on winning arranged PvP.
- Show current training, the proposed effect, stat/total caps, any cost and the actual result in plain language.
- Define how focused training coexists with EVs and experience already earned in ordinary battles. Never silently erase a spread or award the same completed session twice.
- Reuse the existing EV/stat rules and item effects. Training does not raise the existing 252-per-stat / 510-total EV caps or rewrite genetics, nature, moves or Hyper Training rules.

## Affordable retraining

Provide a reliable, inexpensive way to remove or reallocate EV investment so players can try another role or correct incidental battle training. Specify whether the first delivery uses a training service, reliably available EV-reducing berries, or both.

Preview and confirm destructive changes. State the exact affected stats, cost, partial/full reset behavior and HP consequences before committing. A player should not need rare loot, scarce shared stock or a staff reset to experiment with a build.

## Item Finder and training rewards

Keep the original 15-name access inventory explicit: Rare Candy; Bottle Cap; Gold Bottle Cap; Pomeg, Kelpsy, Qualot, Hondew, Grepa and Tamato Berry; Health, Muscle, Resist, Genius, Clever and Swift Feather. Existing vitamins may remain training shortcuts; this does not select a new vitamin source batch.

| Family | Intended role |
| --- | --- |
| Six feathers and existing vitamins | Small boosts or shortcuts; feathers are suitable ordinary Finder rewards. They are not the only route to a finished EV spread. |
| Six EV-reducing berries | Accessible retraining aids, with a reliable route; gathering/growing can supplement it. |
| Rare Candy | Occasional exploration or challenge reward that speeds up leveling. |
| Bottle Cap | Advanced training reward with a reliable progression route alongside rare finds. Preserve the existing level/eligibility rules and stat-only Hyper Training overlay. |
| Gold Bottle Cap | Major milestone reward and optional shortcut; not required for a viable build. |

Choose named Finder rules and eligible locations, with reviewed relative rarity. The currently guarded Potion source does not establish support for arbitrary training-item drops. Preserve its behavior when extending the service. No blanket catalog or item-suffix drop rule, hidden acquisition prerequisite, automatic refill, new currency or tradeable training-credit system is selected by this design.

## Completion

- [ ] Specify the first ordinary Training Grounds location/command flow and a short session or sparring activity, including solo use, meaningful completion, interruption and repeat behavior.
- [ ] Select EV progress, expected sessions for a representative finished spread, any fee and pacing. Show a concrete example using actual PF2 stats and text-battle duration; balance values remain to be chosen rather than inherited from the removed shops.
- [ ] Specify affordable partial/full retraining, confirmation and the interaction with ordinary battle EV/EXP gains.
- [ ] Map all 15 names to reliable access, supplementary finds or optional milestone rewards. Choose Finder weights, locations, repeat limits where needed and advanced training milestones from expected player effort.
- [ ] Define the existing owner/party/current-Fusion, egg, placement, reservation, active-battle, cap and Hyper Training guards. State exact EV/HP, item and wallet effects, preserving no-effect resources and genetic IVs.
- [ ] Create bounded implementation and ordinary-player acceptance follow-ups. Cover train → inspect useful stats → retry/reconnect, retrain → change a battle role, and find/earn → inventory → actual item use.
- [ ] Plan deterministic Finder positive/negative checks separately from real player acquisition; cover stale selection, duplicate completion, interruption, concurrency, post-write rollback and reconnect without duplicate progress/items or lost costs.
- [ ] Compare a trained build in representative NPC and agreed PvP battles. A viable build should be reasonably attainable; winning PvP is not a prerequisite to training it.

Existing finite offers and sales retain their current rules. This design changes no installed stock, room or reward. Keep plot-only items, CAP/fan-content, capture expansion and unrelated work out. Use labelled disposable fixtures for later implementation checks; shared-world installation, migrations, restarts and deployment require their own authorization.

status: Current #952 design replaces the three-counter proposal with Training Grounds, affordable retraining and supplementary Finder/training rewards, following direct user approval. #930 links the revised direction. Existing issue publication receipts remain historical; no runtime/world change is implied.
